# Mosaic

## Placement and release

Relate the cube's observed pose to the tool through the current grasp offset;
slip or regrasping changes that relation. For recessed pockets the complete
rotated cube footprint and bottom seating matter, not only center error. For flat
placement use the task's center and orientation tolerances.

Plan opening and withdrawal with the placement. Dense neighbors can obstruct the
fingertips even when the cube fits: compare grasp height, approach orientation,
placement order, and release near the support surface. Account for the remaining
fall and any movement caused by jaw opening or withdrawal; choose release height
from geometry and evidence, not a fixed drop distance. Placement, release and
withdrawal are separate events. Verify the cube after clearing it.

## Order and rework

The current order and pose affect later grasp access, placement, jaw opening and
withdrawal. Later contact can disturb completed cells: reverify affected results
when evidence changes rather than treating progress as permanent. For correction,
compare regrasping, controlled single or group pushes, temporary removal and
another allocation by contact geometry, observability and total rework cost.
Pushes are ordinary finite moves, not guaranteed alignment; inspect their effect
on neighbors.

## Collaboration

Supply labels establish availability, not ownership. Compare local placement,
direct delivery, handovers and stable staging by reach, congestion, grasp
compatibility, extra handling and concurrent work. For a handover, plan receiver
access and support together with sender release and retreat. Preserve verified
work while enabling independent work with full-arm, payload and opening-finger
clearance.

# Mosaic

## Placement and release

Relate the cube's observed pose to the tool through the current grasp offset;
slip or regrasping changes that relation. For recessed pockets the complete
rotated cube footprint and bottom seating matter, not only center error. For flat
placement use the task's center and orientation tolerances.

Plan opening and withdrawal with the placement. Dense neighbors can obstruct the
fingertips even when the cube fits: compare grasp height, approach orientation,
placement order, and release near the support surface. Account for the remaining
fall and any movement caused by jaw opening or withdrawal; choose release height
from geometry and evidence, not a fixed drop distance. Placement, release and
withdrawal are separate events. Verify the cube after clearing it.

## Order and rework

The current order and pose affect later grasp access, placement, jaw opening and
withdrawal. Later contact can disturb completed cells: reverify affected results
when evidence changes rather than treating progress as permanent. For correction,
compare regrasping, controlled single or group pushes, temporary removal and
another allocation by contact geometry, observability and total rework cost.
Pushes are ordinary finite moves, not guaranteed alignment; inspect their effect
on neighbors.

## Collaboration

Supply labels establish availability, not ownership. Compare local placement,
direct delivery, handovers and stable staging by reach, congestion, grasp
compatibility, extra handling and concurrent work. For a handover, plan receiver
access and support together with sender release and retreat. Preserve verified
work while enabling independent work with full-arm, payload and opening-finger
clearance.

Route regions and arrows indicate progress. Grasp points, handover locations, robot teams, allocation and execution order are planner choices. Independent work may run concurrently.
Grasp the red timber, not a pendant, ring or shaft. Keep the whole assembly clear of table and floor during airborne transport, except for the allowed final GOAL landing.
Any final placement in GOAL is allowed, including cargo contact and stacking. Oracle packing centers and contact-free separation are not task requirements.

Each timber must have at least 70 percent of its centreline length in the vertical space above the GOAL outline. Final completion requires release from every robot; direct or indirect table support is not required.
Only ordinary robot actuators and real contacts may change the live task. No hand welds, object-state writes, hidden-state tools, runtime physics changes or stabilizing attachments.

The initial endpoint chord is 1.20m. The underside fixed eye is 100mm along the timber from its end and directly interlinks with a free eye; the wooden pendant shaft is 170mm long and carries a 600g weight. There is no mounting stem, cable or tray.

# Relay

## Shared payloads

Plan the relative motion of all supporting tools as well as their individual
paths. A same-cycle start does not guarantee matched arrival or prevent internal
loads. Choose support contacts and bearing direction for load moments, not jaw
aperture alone; if a lift changes the payload pose unexpectedly, reassess that
geometry before repeating the motion. Treat support and manipulation as coupled
work: control coupled robots directly together, or give them to one bounded
delegate, rather than splitting coupled support across independent scopes.

## Handovers

Choose teams, the route and handover points from reach, observations and the
cost of each regrasp. Preserve receiver access and sender withdrawal when choosing
a grasp. Before releasing an existing hold, establish the receiver's support from
allowed RGB and robot evidence; width-based grasp feedback alone is insufficient.
Update the shared reference after slip or reorientation.

## At the goal

Check each assembly separately against the completion rule from permitted views,
and confirm that every robot has released it and the jaws have cleared it before
proposing completion. After a drop or collision, reason from the actual scene and
recover with ordinary actions.

# Dial

The robot `ready` tool reports robot capabilities; it is unrelated to the dial
apparatus READY indicator. Before judging table-edge or ring-cutout clearance,
read the geometry reference in `static_workstation`, and use `camera_calibration`
to relate views to the common frame.

## Feedback as evidence

Bind each BEST/READY reading to the timestamped RGB configuration that produced
it, keeping intended settings separate from disk positions you can verify. A
commanded wrist angle describes the tool; the dial's angle belongs to the movable
white disk's frame, which you update after slip or reorientation. An unchanged
BEST does not tell you whether the current input is equal or worse, or which dial
is correct: keep that uncertainty in your note and choose the next experiment from
the observed configuration. Passing through an intermediate stable configuration
can create a valid trial before the commanded target is reached. A contradiction
can come from your assumptions or from execution or observation error.

## Support and manipulation

Derive red operation and blue support from reach, grasp access and commitments;
nominal robot groups describe layout. For a movable module, establish and observe
independent blue-handle support before red contact, and keep the module clear of
external supports. Choose support contact and bearing direction for load moments;
support must resist the partner's reaction forces while preserving approach,
articulation and withdrawal. After support loss, stop the affected operation and
reassess the geometry before re-establishing it.

For an eccentric crank, plan the translating grip point and tool orientation
together in the apparatus frame, and compare approaches with their next
operations: continued turning, partner support, opening and withdrawal. Observe
at useful milestones, since small contact errors change that frame. Keep useful
held settings while other work progresses, counting spring load, drift and the
cost of an occupied gripper.

## Recovery

After a failed move or opening, use the original action's terminal feedback and
selected RGB to distinguish an admission failure, a settled failure and an unknown
outcome. Confirm actual opening and separation before retreating or changing a
supporting grasp; keep sustained support while it is needed.
